note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are registered as the CIL source file in the database.
The CIL compiler parses and resolves the input, building the AST and symbol tables including map classes, permissions, and classmappings.
Map class permissions are created as struct cil_perm with flavor CIL_MAP_PERM and inserted into the map class's perms symtab.
A classmapping statement is parsed, creating a mapping from a map class permission to a list of classperms expressions.
The classperms list in the classmapping is resolved, which may include a CIL_ALL operator referencing another map class.
When the permission expression contains the 'all' operator, the CIL_ALL flavor is appended to the resolved perms list as a CIL_OP item.
The resolved classperms (including the CIL_ALL operation) are appended to the map permission's classperms list.
During pre-verification, the AST walker reaches the CIL_MAP_CLASS node and calls __cil_verify_map_class to verify all its permissions.
Each map class permission is visited; for each, __verify_map_perm_classperms is invoked with the permission's classperms.
The map permission's classperms list is passed to __cil_verify_classperms for recursive verification.
The function iterates over the classperms list, encountering a CIL_CLASSPERMS item whose data is a struct cil_classperms containing a CIL_ALL operation.
The CIL_ALL branch is entered; mc points to the map class referenced by the classperms.
All permissions of the referenced map class are collected into perm_list; each entry's data is a struct cil_perm pointer.

The loop casts j->data to struct cil_perm* unconditionally. If the map class has no own permissions but relies on common permissions, the perm_list is empty and no iteration occurs; however, if the map class has permissions whose classperms contain a recursive CIL_ALL reference, the recursion continues.

The recursive call dereferences cmp->classperms. When the map class has a permission whose classperms list was never initialized (NULL) or contains a malformed entry due to the missing common-permission handling, the read of the classperms pointer or list item data goes out of bounds, causing the heap-buffer-overflow READ 8.
The out-of-bounds read occurs when the recursive call attempts to iterate over an invalid classperms pointer or list item, leading to the ASAN-detected heap-buffer-overflow.
